    // The sum of the positions of the boundary neighbours of a boundary vertex, as
    // a vector. There are exactly two on a well-formed border, so the Loop and
    // Catmull-Clark crease rules read it directly.
    BoundaryNeighborSum(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, boundary: Array<Boolean>, v: Integer): Vector3D
        => topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e => e).Reduce(Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), (acc, e) =>
            topology.IsBoundaryEdge(UndirectedEdgeIndex(e)).And(PairTouches(topology.UndirectedEdges[e], v))
                ? acc + self.Positions[PairOtherEnd(topology.UndirectedEdges[e], v).Value].PositionVector
                : acc);

    // Loop's new point on one edge: 3/8 to each endpoint and 1/8 to each apex, or
    // the midpoint on a boundary edge, which has only one apex.
    LoopEdgePoint(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, e: Integer): Point3D
    {
        var pair = topology.UndirectedEdges[e];
        var near = self.EdgeApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        var far = self.EdgeFarApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        var ends = self.Positions[pair.A.Value].PositionVector + self.Positions[pair.B.Value].PositionVector;
        var apexes = far.IsNone
            ? Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
            : self.Positions[near.Value].PositionVector + self.Positions[far.Value].PositionVector;
        return far.IsNone ? (ends * 0.5).ToPoint : (ends * 0.375 + apexes * 0.125).ToPoint;
    }

    // One level of Loop subdivision: the 1-to-4 topology of a full edge split,
    // with the Loop position rules substituted for the midpoints.
    LoopSubdivided(self: TriangleMesh3D): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        var boundary = self.BoundaryVertexFlags(topology);
        var neighbors = self.VertexNeighborTable(topology);
        var refined = self.SplitEdges(topology, AllEdgesMask(topology));
        var moved = self.Positions.Count
            .MapRange(v => self.LoopVertexPoint(topology, neighbors, boundary, v));
        var inserted = topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e => self.LoopEdgePoint(topology, e));
        return (moved.Concatenate(inserted), refined.Faces);
    }

    // The vertex across the triangle on the far side of a corner's edge — one wing
    // of the Butterfly stencil. The "none" index when that edge is on a boundary.
    WingAcross(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, corner: CornerIndex): VertexIndex
    {
        var twin = topology.CornerTwins[corner.Value];
        return twin.IsNone ? VertexIndex(-1) : self.CornerVertex(PreviousCorner(twin));
    }

    // The sum of the four wing positions of the Butterfly stencil around one edge:
    // the far vertices of the four triangles that touch the edge's two triangles.
    // Returns the "none" answer as a zero vector, which only the regular path uses.
    ButterflyWingSum(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, e: Integer): Vector3D
    {
        var corner = topology.EdgeCorners[e];
        var twin = topology.CornerTwins[corner.Value];
        var wings = [self.WingAcross(topology, NextCorner(corner)),
                     self.WingAcross(topology, PreviousCorner(corner)),
                     self.WingAcross(topology, NextCorner(twin)),
                     self.WingAcross(topology, PreviousCorner(twin))];
        return wings.Reduce(Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), (acc, w) =>
            w.IsNone ? acc : acc + self.Positions[w.Value].PositionVector);
    }

    // True when every vertex the Butterfly stencil needs is present: the edge is
    // interior and so are the four triangles around its two triangles.
    HasFullButterflyStencil(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, e: Integer): Boolean
    {
        var corner = topology.EdgeCorners[e];
        var twin = topology.CornerTwins[corner.Value];
        return twin.IsPresent
            .And(self.WingAcross(topology, NextCorner(corner)).IsPresent)
            .And(self.WingAcross(topology, PreviousCorner(corner)).IsPresent)
            .And(self.WingAcross(topology, NextCorner(twin)).IsPresent)
            .And(self.WingAcross(topology, PreviousCorner(twin)).IsPresent);
    }

    // Butterfly's new point on one edge: 1/2 to each endpoint, 1/8 to each apex and
    // -1/16 to each of the four wings. Where the stencil runs off a boundary the
    // scheme has no rule of its own, so the point falls back to Loop's, which is
    // defined everywhere.
    ButterflyEdgePoint(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, e: Integer): Point3D
    {
        var pair = topology.UndirectedEdges[e];
        var near = self.EdgeApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        var far = self.EdgeFarApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        var ends = self.Positions[pair.A.Value].PositionVector + self.Positions[pair.B.Value].PositionVector;
        var apexes = far.IsNone
            ? Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
            : self.Positions[near.Value].PositionVector + self.Positions[far.Value].PositionVector;
        return self.HasFullButterflyStencil(topology, e)
            ? (ends * 0.5 + apexes * 0.125 - self.ButterflyWingSum(topology, e) * 0.0625).ToPoint
            : self.LoopEdgePoint(topology, e);
    }

    // One level of Butterfly subdivision: the same 1-to-4 topology, the old
    // vertices left exactly where they are, and the eight-point stencil deciding
    // each new one. Interpolating, so the input mesh's vertices lie on the result.
    ButterflySubdivided(self: TriangleMesh3D): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        var refined = self.SplitEdges(topology, AllEdgesMask(topology));
        var inserted = topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e => self.ButterflyEdgePoint(topology, e));
        return (self.Positions.Concatenate(inserted), refined.Faces);
    }

    //==
    // # Catmull-Clark and Doo-Sabin subdivision
    //
    // The two polygon-mesh schemes, both written over the packed corner table of
    // `PolygonMesh3D` (`meshes-polygon.library.plato`). Catmull-Clark
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catmull%E2%80%93Clark_subdivision_surface)
    // is primal: it emits one quadrilateral per corner and after one level every
    // face is a quad. Doo-Sabin
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doo%E2%80%93Sabin_subdivision_surface) is
    // dual: it emits one new vertex per corner and one face per original face,
    // edge and vertex.
    //
    // Both precompute the corner tables below once rather than call the
    // per-corner walks of `meshes-polygon.library.plato`, which are quadratic
    // EACH. That drops a level of subdivision from quartic to quadratic in the
    // corner count. It is still quadratic: subdivision cages are small, and these
    // are for cages.
    //
    // Precondition for the vertex-side rules of both: a closed manifold. The
    // vertex ring of a boundary vertex does not close, and neither scheme's
    // crease rules are implemented here.

    // The face every corner belongs to, in corner order.
    PolygonCornerFaces(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<FaceIndex>
        => self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => f).FlatMap(f => Repeat(self.FaceArity(f), FaceIndex(f)));

    // The next corner around the same face, in corner order. A polygon face wraps
    // at its own arity, so this is NOT the mod-3 step the triangle section uses.
    PolygonNextCorners(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<CornerIndex>
        => self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => f).FlatMap(f =>
            self.FaceArity(f).MapRange(s => self.FaceCorner(f, s + 1)));

    // The vertex every corner points AT, in corner order: the next corner of the
    // same face, wrapping at the end of the row.
    PolygonCornerDestinations(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<VertexIndex>
        => self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => f).FlatMap(f =>
            self.FaceArity(f).MapRange(s =>
                self.Faces.Values[self.Faces.Offsets[f] + (s + 1) % self.FaceArity(f)]));

    // The twin of every corner, from the two corner tables rather than from the
    // mesh: the corner whose own vertex is this one's destination and whose
    // destination is this one's vertex. -1 on a boundary edge.
    PolygonCornerTwins(vertices: Array<VertexIndex>, destinations: Array<VertexIndex>): Array<CornerIndex>
        => vertices.Count.MapRange(c => CornerIndex(vertices.Count
            .MapRange(d => d)
            .Reduce(-1, (found, d) =>
                (vertices[d].Value == destinations[c].Value)
                    .And(destinations[d].Value == vertices[c].Value)
                        ? d
                        : found)));
